step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows First Orion's generative AI setup using Amazon Q to assist cloud operations operators. Generic human actors (User 1, User 2) are pruned per Node Rule 5, leaving AWS IAM Identity Center as the system entry point. Amazon Q acts as a central hub querying multiple data sources (S3 Documentation, Internet Web Crawler, Confluence, and ServiceNow CMDB which receives resource state snapshots from AWS Config). Additionally, Amazon Q connects via action plugins to external services (Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce) to allow users to trigger actions like ticket creation directly from natural language prompts. Services not explicitly named in the AWS vocabulary (Amazon Q, Web Crawler, Confluence, Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce) are normalized to 'ThirdParty', while standard AWS/Partner services use exact vocabulary matches.

graph.name: First Orion Amazon Q Cloud Operations Architecture
graph.notes: First Orion uses Amazon Q published via AWS IAM Identity Center to provide a central web application for cloud operations troubleshooting. It indexes documentation from S3, web crawlers, Confluence, and CMDB data from ServiceNow (fed by AWS Config), while allowing natural language action plugin execution in Jira, Zendesk, and Salesforce.

nodes.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
nodes.notes: System entry point hosting the published Q App where users authenticate.

nodes.name: Amazon Q
nodes.notes: Central generative AI application hub indexing data sources and executing plugins.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 Documentation
nodes.notes: Stores documentation and PDFs indexed by Amazon Q.

nodes.name: Internet Web Crawler
nodes.notes: Data source used to crawl external web domains up to specified link depths.

nodes.name: Confluence
nodes.notes: Knowledge base containing articles and documentation indexed by Amazon Q.

nodes.name: ServiceNow
nodes.notes: CMDB platform queried by Amazon Q for configuration management details.

nodes.name: AWS Config
nodes.notes: Takes state snapshots of AWS resources and synchronizes data to ServiceNow via connector.

nodes.name: Jira
nodes.notes: External plugin integration target for automatic issue and ticket creation.

nodes.name: Zendesk
nodes.notes: External plugin integration target for support ticket creation.

nodes.name: Salesforce
nodes.notes: External plugin integration target for CRM case and data management.

edges.notes: Authenticated user accesses the Q App to send natural language prompts.
Amazon Q reads and indexes documentation from S3.
Amazon Q queries web crawler data source for external web content.
Amazon Q reads knowledge base articles from Confluence.
Amazon Q queries CMDB inventory data in ServiceNow.
AWS Config syncs AWS resource state snapshots into ServiceNow CMDB.
Amazon Q executes action plugin to open a ticket in Jira.
Amazon Q executes action plugin to create a case in Zendesk.
Amazon Q executes action plugin to interact with Salesforce.
